title: Replay job coordinator with idempotent reprocessing and priority queues for console analytics
creator: Jamal Rivera
description: Goal: Build a durable, observable coordinator service + worker pattern that schedules and executes replay/backfill jobs for console usage analytics with strong idempotency guarantees and customer-priority ordering. Background: We've had multiple incidents where schema changes and fixups required reprocessing weeks of events (session grouping bug, missing platform_tag). Existing ad-hoc backfills are manual, error-prone, and lack checkpoints. This ticket scopes a production-grade mechanism to define, schedule, and run reprocessing tasks across large time windows while keeping cost and downstream load under control.
acceptance_criteria: Define a job manifest format that specifies time window, dataset(s), transformations, customer scope, and priority
Coordinator persists jobs and checkpoints (per-customer or shard) so a stopped job resumes without duplicate outputs
Workers implement idempotent write semantics to downstream stores (warehouse, clickhouse, metrics) using event-level dedupe keys
Support priority queues so high-impact customers can be fast-tracked while background reprocesses remain rate-limited
Expose metrics and traces for job progress, per-shard throughput, error rates, and estimated time-to-completion
Can run a small-scale canary job (single-customer, 24h window) and validate outputs against baseline before wide rollout
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Orchestration: chose Temporal for durable long-running workflows and per-job state vs Airflow due to the need for fine-grained retry / child workflows and signal handling
Sharding: use deterministic customer_id hash to shard jobs for parallelism and isolation. Alternative (time-only shards) rejected due to cross-customer hotness.

Deduplication: store event-level write footprint (event_id + output_target) in the dedupe index (TTL) to avoid reapplying transformations; trade-off is extra write/read cost but simplifies correctness
Storage for intermediate state: S3 for large intermediate artifacts (transformed batches) and Postgres for small job metadata/checkpoints
Backpressure: implement token-bucket rate limiter per-worker and per-output-target to throttle downstream writes and avoid cascading failures
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Schema for JobManifest + Temporal workflow scaffold + Postgres tables for jobs/checkpoints. Phase 2: Worker runtime with idempotent write adapters for warehouse and metrics. Phase 3: Priority queue implementation + rate limiting + canary plumbing. Phase 4: Dashboard, alerts, and runbook. Phase 5: Wide-run and postmortem.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Initial scoping and spike approved; created design doc: https://company-confluence.internal/display/ANALY/Replay+Job+Coordinator
2025-02-18: Spike - built Temporal prototype processing 1M events/hour on dev cluster; observed dedupe table lookups added 8% CPU and 12% additional latency per batch
2025-02-22: Design review with infra and security; feedback: add KMS-encrypted S3 buckets for intermediate artifacts and ensure least-privilege IAM roles
2025-02-26: PR opened for Temporal workflows and job schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/7412 (in review)
2025-03-01: Load test results posted: https://grafana.internal/d/analytics/replay-loadtest showing stable throughput at target concurrency with safe throttling enabled
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing and checkpoint logic. Integration test harness that runs a Temporal workflow in CI with an embedded Postgres and S3 mock, validating idempotency by replaying the same event set twice and asserting no duplicates in a test ClickHouse table. A staged canary will be executed against a single internal customer in dev, then a permissive beta in staging before production run.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy coordinator + worker in canary namespace. 2) Create a single-customer 24h canary job with validation hooks. 3) If canary passes, run a prioritized backlog of high-impact customers (manual approval gate). 4) Ramp to medium-priority customers with automated rate limits. 5) Full-run with weekend maintenance window and on-call coverage. Each phase gated by metrics and a manual signoff.
monitoring_and_metrics: Expose metrics: jobs.created, jobs.running, jobs.failed, shards.completed, events.processed/sec, dedupe.hits, dedupe.misses, downstream.write_errors. Dashboards: per-job progress, per-customer ETA, cost-estimate. Alerts: job failure rate > 1% sustained, downstream 5xxs increase > 0.5% above baseline, checkpoint gap increase > 2x expected.
runbook_and_failure_modes: If a worker crashes: Temporal will requeue child workflows; coordinator resumes at last checkpoint.
If downstream write error spikes: automatic pause on affected output target with alert to on-call and circuit-breaker escalation.
If dedupe index grows beyond threshold: disable new large-scale runs and trigger compaction job; notify data infra
